title: Tara and Nibble's Season Surprise
markdown:
Auntie June’s market stall never kept the same face for long. Tara stood on the crate she used as a lookout. Nibble poked his nose from her pocket, whiskers ticking.

Last month the stall had worn pumpkins and knitted hats. Today it wore sparkly strawberries in little boxes and a basket of fluffy chicks that peeped when anyone leaned close.

“Sparkly strawberries,” Nibble squeaked. “Fluffy chicks.”

“Last month, pumpkins and hats,” said Tara. “Why does the stall change?”

Auntie June was tying a paper bag. She did not call anyone dear. She only smiled and set a strawberry where Tara could see the seeds. “Nature keeps a calendar. It does not write on paper.”

Days tiptoed. The sun gave a big, warm hug that stayed and stayed. The stall burst with juicy cherries, yellow peaches, and a pile of sunny fruit that stained Tara’s fingers. She licked a thumb and giggled.

“Plants are hungry for sunshine,” she said.

Nibble counted cherries until he lost his place and started again. Auntie June put a bowl of water under the stall for thirsty dogs. The air smelled sweet and sticky, like jam that had not decided to be jam yet.

Then the sun’s hugs felt less warm. Oranges vanished from the front cloth. Bumpy gourds and red apples took their place, stacked like sleepy hills. The air grew cooler. People came in cozy sweaters. Leaves on the lane turned fiery red and yellow, then danced down and stuck to Tara’s boots.

“Leaves are napping,” Tara squeaked, kicking a little pile so Nibble could ride the rustle.

A breezy afternoon brought plump grapes and a row of warm scarves. Tara pulled her cardigan tight. Nibble shivered in her pocket, so she folded the flap over him like a tiny tent.

“It is chilly,” she said.

“It is,” Auntie June soothed, winding a scarf around a post so it would not blow away. “Do you know why the stall keeps changing its clothes?”

Tara thought. Sunshine. Changing leaves. Cooler air. Strawberries first, then cherries, then apples. Hats once, sweaters now.

“The sun changes how it warms us,” she said. “Warm sun means yummy fruits. Colder means other fruits are ready. And warm clothes keep us snug when it is cold.”

Auntie June beamed and handed her a grape that had already decided to be sweet. “Each special time is a season. Spring is for waking up. Summer for sunshine fruits. Autumn for harvest. Winter for rest. Our clothes keep us just right.”

Tara looked at the stall as if it were a storybook of the year, one page turned every few weeks. “The fruits and clothes are clues for the season.”

“They are,” said Auntie June. She tucked a leftover pumpkin from last month behind the apples, a reminder that the stall remembered its old face.

Nibble poked his head out. “No carrots in winter?” he frowned.

Tara laughed and warmed him with her palm. “Maybe baked apples, Nibble.” She did not ask the stall for other secrets. She bought one apple for now and one for later, and they walked home with leaves still stuck to her boots, the seasons written on the path as clearly as on June’s cloth.
